steps.input: mem = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC shifted-bar marker ray mapping', content='For ARC grids with background filling the canvas, two equal-length horizontal boundary bars of a special color sit at opposite edges, horizontally shifted from each other. Sparse marker pixels lie in the column-span of one bar. For each marker column c in the span of the aligned/source bar starting at s, map its offset to the opposite bar starting at t: target column = t + (c - s). Draw a full vertical stripe of the marker color in every mapped column across the grid, preserving the two boundary bars where they occur. Also extend each original marker vertically toward the boundary bar whose horizontal span contains its column: color the background cells between marker and that bar with the marker color, then recolor the original marker cell to 4. In demos, marker color 0 used special recolor 4; marker color 7 used recolor 4. Example: top bar c16..24, bottom c0..8, marker columns 19,20,21,24 map to c3,4,5,8; source rays point upward to top edge; target stripes fill rows through row0 but stop at bottom boundary bar. Example: top bar c0..6, bottom c7..13, markers at c12,10,13 map to c5,3,6; source rays point down toward bottom bar; target stripes fill rows1..22, preserving top/bottom bars. For a new task, identify bar starts and which bar-span contains each marker; translate marker offsets to the opposite bar. The stripe line should not overwrite boundary-bar cells. Assumption from demonstrated cases: source marker columns fall within one of the bars’ horizontal spans; if a task differs, inspect another demo.', global_=True); print(mem)
